title: Automate changelog and onboard orionx-13b v1.4 (perf metadata + profiles)
author: Priya Rao
description:
Motivation: Onboard orionx-13b v1.4 with curated performance profiles and wire up automated changelog/release-note generation. This PR adds the model metadata for v1.4, new perf profiles for GPU/CPU/quantized configs, and a changelog automation hook that generates release notes from model registry entries and perf profile diffs.

What changed: 1) model metadata: added redwood-models/orionx/13b/v1.4/metadata.json with canonical config, supported quantizations, tokenizer signature, and recommended default serving profile. 2) performance profiles: added per-hardware profiles (a100-40g, a10g, t4, cpu-avx2) and sequence-length buckets (512, 1024, 2048) to profiles/orionx-13b/v1.4/*.json. 3) changelog automation: new GitHub Action workflow .github/workflows/model-changelog.yml that runs on model registry tags and on PR merge; it collects perf-profile diffs and publishes a draft release note in Linear and as a PR comment. 4) tooling: small helper script scripts/registry/changelog_diff.py and updated registry CLI to expose `redwood-registry generate-changelog`. 5) docs: added docs/model-registry/onboarding.md and example rollout snippet for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Checklist:
- [x] metadata file matches registry schema and passes validation
- [x] perf profiles validated against CI benchmark harness
- [x] changelog workflow draft publish tested in staging
- [x] docs updated with rollout guidance

Rollout plan: Merge to main, CI will run perf benchmarks in the staging environment; changelog workflow will produce a draft release to Linear where PM can edit before publishing. Onboarded model will be available in the model catalog behind a feature flag for 24h while we monitor regressions.

Notes: The changelog automation intentionally omits absolute P95 latency numbers from the generated draft (to avoid publishing noisy numbers); it includes relative regressions and configuration recommendations. This PR does not change serving runtime code; it only updates model registry metadata, profiles, tooling, and docs. If any perf regression is detected in CI (>=10% throughput drop vs v1.3) we will block merge (CI enforced) and open ENG-4321 for follow-up.
